title: fix(proxy): fail fast on locally-generated retry hint in capacity-wait loop
body:
## Summary

PR #1000 (`fix(proxy): keep streams alive while account capacity recovers`, merged in v1.20.0) wrapped `_select_account_with_budget_compatible` in a capacity-wait retry loop in both `app/modules/proxy/_service/websocket/mixin.py` and `app/modules/proxy/_service/http_bridge/streaming.py`. The loop sleeps for the duration that `_account_selection_recovery_sleep_seconds_from_message` extracts from the selector's error message, then retries selection.

`select_account` itself formats its no-account error using exactly that shape, via [`_format_retry_hint`](../blob/main/app/core/balancer/logic.py) (`Rate limit exceeded. Try again in <N>s`, capped at `SELECTOR_RETRY_HINT_MAX_SECONDS = 300`). Once every eligible account is `RATE_LIMITED`, the loop matches its own message, waits up to 300s, retries selection, and gets the same message back. The request budget eventually exhausts, but each iteration can hold a request for up to one capped recovery interval.

For single-account deployments this triggers the moment the only account flips to `RATE_LIMITED`: every subsequent request enters the loop and clients hang until the operator restarts the process. This is the reported symptom in #1078 on `v1.20.1`. Multi-account pools hit the same loop whenever every eligible account is simultaneously rate-limited.

This PR short-circuits the locally-generated hint shape in `_account_selection_recovery_sleep_seconds_from_message` so the capacity-wait loop sees `None` and falls through to the normal no-account / rate-limit failure path. Genuine upstream-derived recoverable messages (workspace spend cap, future external `try again in` hints) keep their existing recovery behavior because the prefix match is narrow.

Reporter (@GlowingRuby) deployed the same one-line patch on their single-account instance and confirmed the global-stall behavior is gone; this PR carries that fix and adds the spec / regression coverage.

## What changes

- **Code** (`app/modules/proxy/_service/support.py`): add a `lowered.startswith("rate limit exceeded. try again in")` skip alongside the existing permanent-failure allowlist in `_account_selection_recovery_sleep_seconds_from_message`. One added line; the surrounding allowlist is untouched.
- **Spec** (new `openspec/changes/fix-single-account-rate-limit-hang/`): adds a `responses-api-compat` ADDED Requirement "Locally-generated account-selection retry hints fail fast in capacity wait" with three scenarios (single-account fail-fast, multi-account fail-fast, upstream-derived message still recoverable). Proposal + tasks + spec delta follow the [`add-account-capacity-wait-streaming`](../blob/main/openspec/changes/add-account-capacity-wait-streaming/proposal.md) shape so this change is reviewable alongside the original capacity-wait change.
- **Tests** (`tests/unit/test_proxy_utils.py`): two new direct cases that build the message via `_format_retry_hint(...)` from `app.core.balancer.logic` (capped 300.0 and sub-cap 30.0) so the regression coverage references the real producer and survives a future format change. The existing parametrized permanent-failure cases are untouched.

Diff: +154 / -0 across 5 files. One concern, well under the 800-net-line ceiling.

## Why a new requirement, not a spec edit

`add-account-capacity-wait-streaming` is still an active OpenSpec change folder; modifying its delta would conflict with whoever owns that change. The fail-fast behavior here is also additive (it narrows when the existing "Recoverable account-capacity wait is bounded by the request budget" path runs without removing any scenario), so adding a new requirement scoped to the locally-generated hint shape keeps the spec stack independent.

## To Test

1. **Logic verification (no test environment required)**:
   - [ ] `python3 -c "msg='Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 300s'; print(msg.lower().startswith('rate limit exceeded. try again in'))"` prints `True`.
   - [ ] Same check against the upstream-derived shapes (`You have hit your spend cap...`, `Upstream returned 429: try again in 30s`, `All accounts require re-authentication`, `No fresh additional quota data`) prints `False`.

2. **Unit tests**:
   - [ ] `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_proxy_utils.py -k recovery_sleep -q` passes.
   - [ ] The two new tests `test_account_selection_recovery_sleep_ignores_locally_generated_retry_hint{,_short_wait}` both pass against the patched function.
   - [ ] The existing `test_account_selection_recovery_sleep_ignores_permanent_selection_failures` parametrized cases still pass unchanged.
   - [ ] The recovery-sleep-uses-retry-hint test and the workspace-spend-cap test continue to pass (the prefix match does not steal recoverable messages).

3. **OpenSpec validation**:
   - [ ] `openspec validate fix-single-account-rate-limit-hang --strict` reports no errors.
   - [ ] `openspec validate --specs` continues to pass for `responses-api-compat` after the delta is added.

4. **End-to-end reproduction (against `1.20.1`)**:
   - [ ] Deploy a single-account codex-lb instance.
   - [ ] Generate enough traffic to trigger one real upstream 429 (rate limit, not quota).
   - [ ] Observe that with this patch, the account still goes `RATE_LIMITED` but subsequent requests now fail through the normal rate-limit path instead of hanging until `docker restart`.
   - [ ] Hit the same account directly during the rate-limit window; it should still work (confirming the 429 is real and the loop, not the upstream account, was the stuck component).

## Background

PR #1000 intentionally added the capacity-wait loop to keep streaming clients alive across short upstream wobbles. That goal is preserved here for genuine upstream recoverable signals — the fix only removes the self-feedback case where the proxy waits on its own message. The 300s ceiling on `_format_retry_hint` means the prior behavior could hold a request for up to one capped iteration per loop pass on top of the original `select_account` cooldown, which is what produced the indefinite hangs in the reporter's repro.

The `infer_status_from_usage=False` change from PR #1030 is not the cause of #1078 (the report is about a real upstream 429 that legitimately marks the account `RATE_LIMITED`); the regression is specifically the capacity-wait loop matching its own no-account formatting.

Fixes #1078

title: fix(proxy): surface native transport give-up terminals
body:
fix(proxy): surface native transport give-up terminals

## Summary

Native Codex HTTP Responses requests can receive a committed `200` body, then
lose the upstream stream after codex-lb exhausts its transport attempts. The
proxy used to close that body without a terminal `response.failed` event, so
Codex reported a disconnected stream and retried blindly.

This carrier preserves the internal transport-exhaustion marker through both
native retry gates, then emits exactly one retryable `response.failed` event at
the native Responses boundary. It also closes the suspended async-generator
chain so the retry layer releases its account lease instead of accumulating
`account_stream_cap` failures. The original internal transport code remains
the account-health and request-log classification; `rate_limit_exceeded` is an
egress-only Codex retry signal.

## Scope

- The canonical `Please try again in <N>s.` hint is placed first so Codex's
  reconnect parser cannot consume a competing upstream hint.
- Unmarked raw EOF, local pre-dispatch refusals, non-native Responses shaping,
  and internal transport/account-health codes retain their existing behavior.
- No WebSocket overload relabeling or denied-anchor `request_submit.py` change
  is included; those are separate review surfaces.
- The contract and scenarios live in
  `openspec/changes/native-codex-giveup-terminal/`.

This is a maintainer-owned adaptation of the useful native-terminal work in
https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/2396, with credit retained for its
original author, Gabe Bryk (`@gabrielbryk`). It addresses the lease-release
failure reported in https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/issues/2470.

Fixes #2470

## Validation

- `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_proxy_utils.py` — 1419 passed
- `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_proxy_api_responses_contract.py` — 86 passed
- `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_proxy_http_bridge.py tests/unit/test_streaming_retry_virtual_time.py tests/unit/test_responses_streaming_timeout_hardening.py tests/integration/test_proxy_transient_retry.py` — 1137 passed
- `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, and `uv run ty check` — passed
- OpenSpec change validation — valid; all 66 current specs — passed

The repository-wide architecture command reaches the existing base-branch
migration-topology failure: two `20260914_000000` heads are present on
`origin/main`. This change adds no migrations; the other architecture,
cancellation, timing-seam, and settings checks pass.

title: fix(proxy): classify Windows route errors 1231/1232 as host network loss
body:
## Summary

Classify typed Windows `winerror` 1231 (`ERROR_NETWORK_UNREACHABLE`) and 1232 (`ERROR_HOST_UNREACHABLE`) as host network loss. They then take the account-neutral shared-client recovery path that `ENETUNREACH`/`EHOSTUNREACH` already take on POSIX. Winerror 64 (`ERROR_NETNAME_DELETED`) and 121 (`ERROR_SEM_TIMEOUT`) stay account and endpoint attributed, with no shared-client rotation, as `ECONNRESET`/`ETIMEDOUT` do on POSIX.

## Type of change

- [x] `fix:` — bug fix (no behavior change beyond the bug)
- [ ] `feat:` — new user-facing feature or capability
- [ ] `refactor:` — internal refactor
- [ ] `docs:` — documentation only
- [ ] `chore:` / `ci:` / `build:`
- [ ] `test:` — test-only change
- [ ] Breaking change

Linked issue: Fixes #2456

## OpenSpec

- [x] This PR includes / updates an OpenSpec change
- [ ] Not applicable — bug fix that matches the existing spec
- [ ] Not applicable — docs / CI / chore only
- [ ] This PR touches a codex-faithful path and preserves upstream-equivalent behavior

Change directory: `openspec/changes/classify-windows-route-errors/`

## Changes

- `app/core/resilience/network_recovery.py`: `is_process_network_failure` also matches typed `winerror` 1231/1232. Message text never matches.
- The rule is POSIX parity. A Windows code is neutral only when it is the Windows form of an errno main already treats as neutral. 64/121 map to `ECONNRESET`/`ETIMEDOUT`, so they stay attributed.
- The pre-dispatch replay gate is unchanged. Only a typed connector error permits a same-account retry.
- Tests use a typed `WindowsOSError` subclass (`tests/unit/_proxy_test_helpers.py`), so they type-check on every platform.
- The OpenSpec delta records the parity rule, a code-by-code table, the evidence, and one known residual gap (aiohappyeyeballs multi-address collapse, same as POSIX).

## Evidence

- CPython `PC/errmap.h` `winerror_to_errno` passes Winsock codes 10000-11999 through as errno, so `WSAENETUNREACH` and the other WSA route codes already match main. 64, 121, 1231 and 1232 have no case and fall to `default: return EINVAL`.
- `Modules/overlapped.c` `Overlapped.getresult` raises the `GetOverlappedResult` Win32 error. `Lib/asyncio/windows_events.py` `finish_connect` re-raises it unchanged. `finish_socket_func` turns `ERROR_NETNAME_DELETED` into `ConnectionResetError`.
- Local run, CPython 3.13.4, Windows 11, `ProactorEventLoop.sock_connect`:
  - `0.1.2.3:443`, `240.0.0.1:443` -> winerror 1231, errno 22
  - `224.0.0.1:443` -> winerror 1232, errno 22
  - `192.0.2.1:443`, `10.255.255.1:443` -> winerror 121, errno 22 (connect timeout, host online)
  - `127.0.0.1:1` -> winerror 1225 (`ConnectionRefusedError`)

## Simplicity

- [x] Works with zero configuration.
- [x] Adds no required setup step.
- New settings: none.
- [x] README, `.env.example`, and dashboard navigation are unchanged.

## Test plan

Run locally on Windows 11, CPython 3.13.4.

```text
uv run ruff check .
All checks passed!

uv run ruff format --check .
1301 files already formatted

uv run ty check --python-platform linux
2 diagnostics, both `uvloop` unresolved imports in untouched files
(scripts/bench_native_websocket.py, tests/unit/test_runtime_logging_loop_handler.py).
uvloop cannot be installed on Windows. 0 diagnostics in changed files.

uv run pytest tests/unit/test_network_recovery.py tests/unit/test_http_client.py -q
63 passed

uv run pytest tests/unit/test_proxy_utils.py -q -k "windows or raw_route"
5 passed

uv run pytest tests/integration/test_proxy_transient_retry.py -q --timeout 60
63 passed

npx --yes @fission-ai/openspec@1.11.0 validate --specs
Totals: 66 passed, 0 failed

npx --yes @fission-ai/openspec@1.11.0 validate --type change --strict --no-interactive -- classify-windows-route-errors
Change 'classify-windows-route-errors' is valid

python3 .github/scripts/check_simplicity_budgets.py
all budgets OK

python .github/scripts/check_all_contributors.py
all-contributors covers 119 GitHub commit contributors
```

Mutation check: with 64/121 put back in the classified set, all 6 parity tests fail (unit classifier, `stream_responses` breaker and error code, route-level no-rotation).

The full unit slice (`tests/unit tests/simulation tests/test_request_logs_options_api.py`, `-n 8`) ran on this branch (before the final test-only fold, same app code) and on clean `origin/main`. Both show the same 145 failed + 2 errors, all Windows-environment failures. The failure lists match exactly, so none are new.

## Screenshots / output

No dashboard change. Route-level regressions:

- Connector-wrapped 1231/1232 rotates the failed client and completes once on the same account.
- Raw 1231/1232 rotates the client for later callers and surfaces `proxy_network_unavailable` without replay, account-health change, or breaker write.
- Raw 64/121 records the account circuit-breaker failure, returns `upstream_unavailable`, and does not rotate the shared client.

title: fix(proxy): keep frameless bridge drops account neutral
body:
## Current Review Status

Synced upstream main in 65629172. Missing native capabilities fail closed as NativeEgressProtocolError; non-container installs must rebuild the native helper for websocket_close_frame_provenance_v1. Protocol-error replay eligibility retains existing upstream guards; this PR does not add a no-replay gate for accepted output-free protocol failures.

The proposed removal of post-output drain and soft error-rate signals still requires an explicit upstream owner decision. The author's rationale is not owner approval.

This exact head will not be deployed or production load-tested. Production remains on the previously tested stable build.

## Summary

Keep terminal HTTP bridge WebSocket losses without an upstream-authored close
frame account-neutral even after response events or buffered model output have
started. Request progress still blocks transparent replay, while explicit
transport-ending provenance prevents protocol errors from being mistaken for
socket loss.

Fixes #2074

## Type of change

- [x] `fix:` ΓÇö bug fix (no behavior change beyond the bug)
- [ ] `feat:` ΓÇö new user-facing feature or capability
- [ ] `refactor:` ΓÇö internal refactor (no behavior change, no API change)
- [ ] `docs:` ΓÇö documentation only
- [ ] `chore:` / `ci:` / `build:` ΓÇö tooling, CI, packaging
- [ ] `test:` ΓÇö test-only change
- [ ] **Breaking change**

Linked issue: Fixes #2074; follow-up to #1754.

Related reports:

- Refs #1754: direct predecessor for account-health penalties from frame-less
  eventless drops; this PR extends the same attribution rule after output.
- Related to #1711: its production evidence includes upstream mid-turn closes
  after positive first-event latency. This PR prevents account-health
  amplification but does not prevent the underlying socket interruption or
  change cleanup budgets.
- Related to #1707: this PR prevents one transport-triggered route into the
  `stream_incomplete` -> owner-backoff -> owner-unavailable cascade. It does
  not migrate continuations whose owner is genuinely dead or quota-exhausted.

## OpenSpec

- [x] This PR includes / updates an OpenSpec change
- [ ] Not applicable ΓÇö bug fix that matches the existing spec
- [ ] Not applicable ΓÇö docs / CI / chore only
- [x] This PR touches a codex-faithful path and preserves upstream-equivalent behavior

Change directory: `openspec/changes/keep-frameless-midstream-drops-account-neutral/`

## Changes

- Classify terminal close/error messages with no close frame (`None` or
  adapter-synthesized `1006`) as transport evidence regardless of response
  progress.
- Keep the interrupted request fail-closed as `stream_incomplete`; visible or
  buffered output still prohibits replay.
- Keep the windowed eventless account signal restricted to zero events and no
  buffered output.
- Mark buffered-output durable operations acknowledged so reconnect cannot
  redispatch them.
- Add positive `transport_ended` provenance to WebSockets, aiohttp/Codex, and
  native-egress adapters; protocol-invalid nonterminal messages retain the
  safe default `False` and remain account-attributable.
- Cover account-health writes, send count, SSE terminal shape, buffered-output
  operation state, protocol errors, and each supported adapter.

## Production evidence

This was diagnosed from an instrumented production deployment based on
`v1.25.0-beta.1` under ongoing concurrent OpenCode traffic. Identifiers below
are intentionally omitted.

- Two active upstream WebSockets vanished without close frames after 3 and 9
  response events respectively.
- Both requests had visible or buffered model output and correctly terminated
  as `stream_incomplete`; replay would have risked duplicate output, billing,
  or tool effects.
- On the old behavior, repeated frame-less losses incremented account
  `error_count`; crossing the threshold stranded continuity-bound follow-ups as
  `previous_response_owner_unavailable` while another pool account was healthy.
- EC2 status checks remained healthy, CPU peaked around 52%, CPU credits were
  available, and the active failure reproduced after resizing from 2 GiB to
  4 GiB RAM, which ruled out host exhaustion as the primary cause.

An equivalent Python bridge patch was then exercised on the same deployment
under continuing load. A later frame-less loss after 3 events:

- remained `stream_incomplete`;
- requested no account-health penalty;
- emitted no eventless account signal;
- performed no transparent redispatch;
- allowed the affected client session to continue on a later request;
- left local and public readiness at HTTP 200.

The upstream-focused branch additionally covers the native-egress adapter that
was added on current `main`; that current-main-only adapter was validated
locally rather than claimed as part of the beta deployment.

## Simplicity

- [x] Works with zero config and changes no default or required setup step.
- New setting(s): none.
- [x] No README, `.env.example`, dashboard navigation, schema, or migration changes.

## Test plan

```text

# 154 passed

uv run pytest tests/integration/test_http_responses_bridge.py::test_v1_responses_http_bridge_stream_failure_remains_valid_sse
# 3 passed

uv run pytest tests/unit/test_proxy_http_bridge.py -k \
  "abrupt_eventless_drop_stays_account_neutral or abrupt_drop_after_response_events_stays_account_neutral or abrupt_drop_after_buffered_reasoning_prelude_stays_account_neutral or protocol_error_without_transport_ending_still_penalizes_account or reader_failure_classifies_each_operation_from_its_own_events"
# 5 passed

uv run pytest tests/unit/test_proxy_websocket_client.py -k \
  "native_direct_adapter or live_direct_adapter_preserves_abnormal_close_code_and_reason or direct_adapter_classifies_keepalive_timeout or routed_adapter_classifies_heartbeat_timeout"
# 7 passed

uv run python scripts/check_proxy_architecture.py
uv run python scripts/check_cancellation_safety.py
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
```

title: fix(proxy): bound memory used by paused bridge streams
body:
## Summary

A client that stops reading an HTTP Responses stream leaves upstream output accumulating in an unbounded queue. This bounds the retained live output while preserving ordered delivery and cleanup.

Closes #2266.

## Changes

- Use a two-event queue with a 256 MiB process-wide live-payload budget, including blocked producers.
- Release reservations and wake blocked producers on cancellation or detach. Keep persistence, replay and API-key settlement intact.
- After deadline-related output loss, deliver the retained prefix followed by `response.failed` and end-of-stream instead of reporting success.

The HTTP bridge retains its native-egress bypass pending acceptance. Other WebSocket transports keep their native default. No new setting is added.

OpenSpec: [bounded bridge event queue](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/tree/2df95e7d18cf51d220282a27fb29b67a89441cd0/openspec/changes/bound-http-bridge-event-queue). Related historical work: #1840 and #1867.

## Test plan

At `2df95e7d1`, 2,770 affected bridge, error, queue-lifecycle, settings-removal and HTTP Responses integration tests passed against the composition with current main `aae61f6f`. Both database URLs and the main/background/fixture engines used the same dedicated disposable SQLite database. PostgreSQL and native helper execution remain hosted checks.

A negative control using the unshielded upstream detach call fails all four HTTP/SSE and cancellation ownership regressions. The composition retains the shielded helper and passes those cases. It also preserves upstream's removal of optional recovery modes.

Full Ruff lint/format, typing, architecture/cancellation/timing/settings guards, strict OpenSpec 1.11.0 validation of the change and all 65 main specs pass. Independent Astra Medium review found no actionable composition findings. This review covers the new merge and its affected behavior, not a fresh review of the whole historical PR. [Current hosted checks](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/1903/checks) remain part of the merge gate.

## Remaining acceptance

The [maintainer disposition](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/1903#issuecomment-5614055969) accepts the 256 MiB limit as a live queued-payload bound, including blocked producers. Aggregate completed replays and total process memory are outside that boundary; completed replay retains its separate spool contract.

Bounded per-request delivery-stall termination, retained-prefix delivery followed by failure/EOS, reservation release, and same-session sibling progress are accepted requirements. The numeric maximum continuous delivery stall remains maintainer-owned. The current implementation still waits until the request deadline, up to two hours, so #2266 remains unfinished. The OpenSpec change records the missing proof without selecting a duration.

Native HTTP-bridge bypass and residual performance acceptance remain separate. Local queue benchmarks do not establish production throughput or native transport acceptance.
